questions.question: How should you check your blind spots before changing lanes?

options.text: Turn your head quickly to look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head quickly to look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your vehicle and others?

options.text: It prevents distractions from other vehicles.
It gives you time to react if something unexpected happens.
It keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.
It keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react if something unexpected happens.
questions.explanation: Space between vehicles gives you time to react to mistakes other drivers make.

questions.question: How do you know you are parked at a safe distance behind another vehicle?

options.text: You can read its license plate.
You can see the ground under the vehicle's rear wheels.
You can read its bumper stickers.
You can count the number of passengers in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see the ground under the vehicle's rear wheels.
questions.explanation: When parked behind another vehicle, stay back far enough that you can see the ground under its rear wheels. This distance lets you move around the vehicle safely and protects you if the car rolls backward.

questions.question: When is it okay to honk your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you have lost control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to the danger.

questions.question: What must you do if a train is close enough or fast enough to be dangerous?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Wait until the train has completely passed before crossing the tracks.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find an alternative route across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the train has completely passed before crossing the tracks.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is near or moving fast enough to be dangerous, do not cross. This is true even if there are no signals or they are not working.

questions.question: What does a green arrow with a red light mean?

options.text: You may only drive straight ahead.
You may only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to proceed.
All vehicles must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction of the arrow, and only if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.
Don't park on the right side of the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is not allowed. In this case, right turns are not permitted.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
As you decrease your speed, the roadway becomes more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on a wet road, the less grip your tires have. At high speeds, your tires may lose contact with the road and slide on water, a condition called hydroplaning.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to let the bicyclist know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane to get around them.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed up to get in front of the bicyclist quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: When passing a bicycle, slow down and give as much space as possible. Bicyclists have less protection than drivers. Passing too quickly can make them lose control.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
The road curves ahead.
There are upcoming intersections.
There is road construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane on a multilane road will end. Traffic in the right lane must move to the left lane.

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows to control turns from specific lanes. What does a solid red arrow mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a circular red traffic light.
It means drivers may turn in the direction the arrow points.
It means traffic in that direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a circular red traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same thing as a circular red light. Traffic in that lane must stop and cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit in a business district if no other speed limit is posted?

options.text: 70 mph
55 mph
40 mph
30 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 30 mph
questions.explanation: The speed limit in a business district is 30 miles per hour. Follow any posted speed limit signs if they show a different speed.

questions.question: What should drivers do when preparing to turn left?

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking the rearview mirror.
Move into the left lane.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When turning left, signal three to five seconds before the turn. Check your rearview mirror and slow down gradually. On a multilane road, move into the left lane before the intersection. Yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and turn when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do if you encounter an aggressive driver?

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Tailgate them in return.
Make sure they know you disapprove of their behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If another driver is driving dangerously or threatening you, stay calm. Slow down and let them pass. Put distance between your vehicles. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: When can you safely pass on a two-way, two-lane street?

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle can go fast enough to pass.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You can only pass safely when you can clearly see the road, you can return to your lane before oncoming traffic arrives, and your vehicle is fast enough to pass. Never pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: If someone is injured in an accident you are involved in, what should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away immediately.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless necessary. Moving them incorrectly can make injuries worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, use direct pressure to stop it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Lane closed ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black symbols on a yellow background. They alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns that a traffic signal is ahead. Be ready to stop at a red or yellow light.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Go the same speed.
Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: Slow down when a driver wants to pass. This creates space in front of your vehicle, making it easier and faster for them to complete the pass safely.

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign mean?

options.text: A no passing zone is starting.
A railroad crossing is ahead.
A school zone is ahead.
Construction work is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work is present.
questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols indicate construction, maintenance, or emergency work.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Human error
Bad weather
Bad roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Human error
questions.explanation: Crashes often happen when drivers do not see other vehicles or when they drive unexpectedly. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what can you do?

options.text: You can still turn, but you must let oncoming traffic go first.
You cannot turn anymore and must go straight.
You still have the right to turn.
You do not have to turn in the arrow's direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can still turn, but you must let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you may still turn in the arrow's direction. However, you must yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic first.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots before changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Use the outside rearview mirror.
Use both the inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Always turn your head to check your blind spots before you change lanes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
The divided highway is ending.
Two-way traffic.
Keep left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The divided highway is ending.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about upcoming hazards. This sign tells you that the divided highway will end soon.

questions.question: Can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public road?

options.text: Yes, as long as you are not driving.
Yes, if you are in the back seat.
Yes, if you are in the back of a pickup truck.
No, never.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or have open alcohol in any vehicle on a public road. You cannot have open alcohol containers in the front or back seat, or anywhere in the vehicle on a public road.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: It is summer.
You must stop and back up immediately.
Road conditions are not ideal for driving.
You should drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions are not ideal for driving.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange. They tell you that work is being done on or near the road. Drive with extra care when you see these signs.

questions.question: What should you do if there is an oncoming car on the left and a cyclist on the right?

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder.
Drive between both of them.
Let the car pass first, then pass the cyclist.
Pass the cyclist quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass first, then pass the cyclist.
questions.explanation: When you face multiple hazards, handle one at a time. Let the oncoming car pass, then pass the cyclist. Do not try to squeeze between both at the same time.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, what must you do?

options.text: Keep your normal speed.
Stop and look for police cars.
Let pedestrians go first.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians go first.
questions.explanation: You can turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says otherwise. When turning, you must yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a yellow traffic light?

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep going because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
See what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming. Stop unless you have already entered the intersection.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, what should you expect?

options.text: They know when it is safe to cross.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They may run in front of you without looking.
They will not cross unless an adult is with them.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may run in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be careful in areas where children play. Children may not understand danger and can run in front of your car without looking.

questions.question: At a stop sign, after you stop, what should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for tailgating cars.
Move when the car ahead of you moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because traffic from the left is closer to you. Then look right, then look left again in case you missed a vehicle.
